questions.q: What does a standard Receivables invoice typically debit and credit?
questions.explain: A standard invoice debits the Receivable account and credits Revenue for the invoiced amount.

questions.q: What does SO-48217's $2,755.00 credit memo do to the accounting from the original invoice?
options: It reverses part of the original entry: debits Revenue and credits Receivable
It adds an entirely new, unrelated revenue entry
It debits Cash and credits Revenue
It has no accounting effect at all
questions.explain: The credit memo partially reverses the original invoice entry, reducing both revenue and the receivable.

questions.q: When Harborview's cash receipt is applied, what accounts are affected?
options: Only the General Ledger suspense account
Cash and Receivable (revenue is not touched again)
questions.explain: Applying the receipt debits Cash and credits Receivable; revenue was already recognized at invoicing and isn't touched again.

questions.q: What generates these journal entries in Oracle Fusion?
options: A person manually typing debits and credits for every transaction
Subledger Accounting rules reacting automatically to Receivables business events
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting (SLA) rules automatically generate the appropriate journal entries for each defined business event.

questions.q: After all three entries (invoice, credit memo, cash receipt), what is the net balance in the Receivable account for this specific invoice?
questions.explain: $55,100.00 debit minus $2,755.00 credit minus $52,345.00 credit nets to $0.00 — fully cleared.
